Your rank comes from how far through each of your own exercises you have got, compared against that exercise\'s full range. The typical exercise decides it, and recent training counts for more than old training. Train at least 5 different exercises to unlock it.
This is your rank across all the strength exercises you train, measured by how far through each one you have got. Higher means you are training at harder levels.
Your rank works out like a GPA for strength training. It is worked out by:
Looking at every strength exercise you have trained.
Measuring how far through its own range each one is — exercises have very different lengths, so this compares progress, not raw levels.
Taking the middle exercise, with the ones you trained most recently counting for more.

The level system in one picture
Every exercise climbs its own ladder of levels. You train 3 working sets — the reps show how close you are to the next level.
Each exercise has its own levels. Higher levels mean more resistance or a harder variation.
Within a level, you progress through stages by adding reps \u2014 one rep on every set at once, so 8 / 8 / 8 becomes 9 / 9 / 9.
When you finish the last stage, you move up a level and start again at lower reps with more load.
If the next load is a big jump, the app resets your reps to make it manageable.
Tap the lock on the level card to hold THIS exercise on its current level \u2014 it stays where it is even after a finished workout, and the level box stops offering a change. Tap it again to unlock.
